expectations.text: Recommends bootnet::estimateNetwork or qgraph::EBICglasso as the estimation function
expectations.evidence: Response recommends `estimateNetwork()` from bootnet explicitly in code: `net <- estimateNetwork(df, default = "EBICglasso", ...)` and notes 'bootnet wraps qgraph and handles estimation + all the accuracy machinery. You rarely need to call qgraph::EBICglasso directly.'

expectations.text: Uses or recommends corMethod='cor_auto' or polychoric correlations (not Pearson) for the Likert items
expectations.evidence: Code uses `corMethod = "cor_auto"` and the response explains: 'With 0–4 scales, Pearson correlations systematically underestimate the associations — this is one of the most common errors in published networks. cor_auto handles it automatically.'

expectations.text: Mentions tuning parameter / gamma (typically 0.5) for EBIC
expectations.evidence: Code sets `tuning = 0.5` with explanation: 'The EBIC gamma controls sparsity... 0.5 is the field default per Epskamp & Fried (2018) and what reviewers expect unless you have a strong reason to deviate.'

expectations.text: Recommends accuracy and stability checks via bootnet() bootstrapping as a required next step, not optional
expectations.evidence: Sections 6 and 7 are explicitly labeled 'Edge accuracy — non-negotiable step 1' and 'Centrality stability — non-negotiable step 2', with full bootnet() code for both nonparametric and case-dropping bootstraps.

expectations.text: Refers to the canonical tutorial paper (Epskamp, Borsboom & Fried 2018 in Behavior Research Methods) OR points the user to a comparable canonical resource (e.g. Isvoranu et al. 2022 textbook). Naming any of these authors in a substantive way counts.
expectations.evidence: Final paragraph: 'The canonical reference for the full pipeline is Epskamp, Borsboom & Fried (2018) in Behavior Research Methods (freely available) — worth keeping open alongside this as you work through it.'

expectations.text: Does NOT recommend reporting closeness or betweenness centrality without caveat
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly states: 'Do not report closeness or betweenness — they are inappropriate for weighted partial-correlation graphs and typically unstable (Bringmann et al., 2019).' This is an unambiguous prohibition, not a caveated recommendation.
